title: Turn sign-in on for make dev with one command
request: I got this error again: sign-in, members and several workspaces come on with DCLAB_AUTH. Fix it simply, to have login in the R&D project.
spec: Accounts need PostgreSQL and DCLAB_AUTH; the first owner is made from the command line, the password never an argument.
plan: One command that gets dclab_dev ready, writes DCLAB_AUTH=password to .env once and makes the first owner
Point the page's messages at it

decisions.decision: make login asks for the email and the password itself.
decisions.why: A password typed by the owner never reaches a shell history or a session.

decisions.decision: A sign-in already set in .env is never changed.
decisions.why: The owner may use the identity provider instead.

change: scripts/dev.py (login, enable_login), Makefile (login), the workspace switcher's and the Admin members page's messages, tests/test_dev_script.py.

findings.defect: Turning sign-in on took several steps the page did not name.
findings.scenario: The owner clicked the workspace switcher and read that sign-in comes on with DCLAB_AUTH, with no command to run.
findings.cause: The setting, the database and the first owner were three separate steps documented only in .env.example.
findings.fix: make login does all three; the messages name it.

outcome: One command turns sign-in on; friends are added on the Admin page.
lessons: A message that names a setting should name the command that sets it.
